steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.

Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.

title: When Do Typed Decision Models Work in Transportation? Evidence from Travel Choice and Traffic Signal Control
summary: Typed decision models replace free-form chat-based LLM generation with a structured interface that directly returns an action and an option-level probability distribution, substituting for both chat LLMs and, potentially, conventional discrete choice or reinforcement learning controllers. They cost less in inference latency and compute than chat-based LLMs and are accessible via third-party APIs, but the paper reports lower prediction accuracy than traditional discrete choice models and the strongest chat baseline, representing a quality trade-off. They can fail through sensitivity to input representation and question framing, and they degrade under challenging traffic network conditions, so robustness evaluation per deployment scenario is necessary.
rationale: The method offers a credible latency and cost reduction over chat-based LLMs through existing APIs, but its accuracy deficit and sensitivity to input framing require validation on the reader's specific decision tasks before production use.
technique: Typed decision models for structured LLM decisions

They cost less in inference latency and compute than chat-based LLMs and are accessible via third-party APIs, but the paper reports lower prediction accuracy than traditional discrete choice models and the strongest chat baseline, representing a quality trade-off. They can fail through sensitivity to input representation and question framing, and they degrade under challenging traffic network conditions, so robustness evaluation per deployment scenario is necessary.

Typed decision models achieve lower inference latency and computational cost than evaluated chat-based LLMs, but with lower prediction accuracy than traditional discrete choice models and the strongest chat-based baseline on Swissmetro, and performance degradation under challenging traffic control conditions.
